title: Constructing Non-Hermitian Theories with Tunable Exceptional Points and Controlled State Purification
authors: Soumya Kanti Pal, Rupak Majumder, Shamik Gupta
abstract: Exceptional points (EP's) are a hallmark of non-Hermitian quantum systems. We show that momentum-space deformation provides a general design principle for creating and controlling EP's in quadratic many-body Hamiltonians. We identify universal criteria for the momentum sectors to host EP's and the corresponding critical deformation strengths, while revealing that a single momentum-sector EP induces quite remarkably an exponential proliferation of many-body eigenvector coalescences. We further establish EP's as a universal mechanism for purifying arbitrary mixed quantum states, uncovering distinct purification regimes and a fundamental odd-even system-size dichotomy in the thermodynamic limit. Our framework also provides a systematic reverse-engineering protocol for generating short- and long-range, reciprocal and nonreciprocal non-Hermitian quantum matter, together with an explicit Lindblad embedding. These results thus establish momentum-space deformation as a unified route to exceptional-point engineering and controlled design of many-body non-Hermitian quantum systems.
summary: The paper presents a comprehensive framework using momentum-space deformation to design non-Hermitian Hamiltonians exhibiting tunable Exceptional Points. These EPs are shown to act as universal mechanisms capable of purifying arbitrary mixed quantum states. The results provide systematic protocols for engineering various types of non-Hermitian quantum matter.
main_problem: The work develops a general design principle for creating and controlling Exceptional Points (EPs) in quadratic many-body Hamiltonians, while also establishing EPs as a universal mechanism for purifying arbitrary mixed quantum states.
main_result: Momentum-space deformation provides a unified route to engineer EPs, which fundamentally allows for the purification of mixed quantum states, exhibiting distinct odd-even system-size dichotomies in the thermodynamic limit.
method: The analysis uses momentum-space decomposition of quadratic fermionic Hamiltonians and introduces non-Hermitian deformations ($\mathbf{H}_{	ext{nH}, k} = \mathbf{H}^{(1)} - i\mathbf{H}^{(2)}$) to systematically tune parameters towards EP conditions.
model_or_system: The primary model is the quadratic free fermionic Hamiltonian (e.g., Transverse Field Ising Chain), analyzed in momentum space via Bloch Hamiltonians $\hat{H}_k$. The non-Hermiticity is introduced through controlled deformations ($\gamma$).
key_observables: Normalized purity $P(t)$, eigenvalue/eigenvector coalescence, and the existence of EPs at critical deformation strengths ($\gamma^{(c)}$).
important_parameters: Deformation strength $\gamma$ relative to critical thresholds ($\gamma^{(1)}_c, \gamma^{(2)}_c$), system size parity (odd vs. even $L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to quadratic BdG Hamiltonians; purification proofs rely on the existence of a Jordan canonical form structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometric conditions for EPs in parameter space and show the exponential proliferation of eigenvector coalescences induced by an EP within a single momentum block.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general framework using momentum-space deformation, details the EP criteria, demonstrates state purification dynamics across different deformation regimes ($\gamma$), and concludes with protocols for engineering various non-Hermitian couplings (short/long-range).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems by providing a powerful tool (EPs) to engineer dissipation or coherence control, which is highly relevant for understanding decoherence and state preparation in complex physical platforms.
